title: Modeling Repair of Intestinal Damage with Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Organoids
author: Skarp, Yetkin-Arik, et al.

steps.title: Maintain aseptic conditions
steps.instruction: Perform all steps inside a laminar flow hood, keep cells on ice unless otherwise stated, verify cells are mycoplasma‑negative, and incubate all culture steps at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Prepare conditioned media
steps.instruction: Follow Vonk et al. 5 to generate Wnt‑3A‑conditioned medium (WCM) and Noggin‑conditioned medium (NCM); this preparation takes approximately 3 weeks. Commercial Wnt‑3A (e.g., ImmunoPrecise or SinoBiological) and Noggin (powder or frozen NCM) are available but increase cost.

steps.title: Prepare MSC growth medium
steps.instruction: Prepare MSC growth medium (≈30 min total) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 50 µg basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) in 5 ml PBS, aliquot into ten 500 µl tubes (10 µg ml⁻¹), and store at –20 °C (avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles).
Dissolve 0.579 g L‑ascorbic acid phosphate in 40 ml demi‑water to obtain a 50 mM solution.
Combine the above reagents with the remaining MSC medium components and sterile‑filter the complete medium through a 0.22 µm (or 0.45 µm) membrane.

steps.title: Seed organoids and apply busulfan
steps.instruction: Seed the established human duodenal organoid line in 10 µl Matrigel droplets (≈500 cells per droplet) in a 24‑well plate, treat each droplet with busulfan (DNA‑alkylating cytotoxin) for the desired exposure time, then remove busulfan by washing.

steps.title: Introduce MSCs and culture
steps.instruction: Add the prepared MSCs to each Matrigel droplet after busulfan removal and culture the co‑culture at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for several days (exact duration defined by the experiment).

steps.title: Capture bright‑field images
steps.instruction: Acquire light‑microscope images (≈2 h total) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Place the organoid plate under a microscope and select the 1.25× objective.
Adjust focus until most organoids are in focus and capture a bright‑field image of each droplet.
Include a scalebar in every image to enable pixel‑to‑micrometer conversion.

steps.title: Determine image scale in Fiji
steps.instruction: Open each image with the scalebar in Fiji, measure the scale, and record the pixel‑to‑micrometer ratio (e.g., for an EVOS M5000: 346 px / 2000 µm at 1.25×, 358 px / 550 µm at 4×).

steps.title: Segment organoids using OrganoSeg
steps.instruction: Process the images with OrganoSeg (download from https://github.com/JanesLab/OrganoSeg) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Launch OrganoSeg and select File → Open → New Image Set; load up to 72 images.
Check “Out‑of‑Focus Correction”.
In the Spheroid Editing Toolbar click “Split” as needed.
Set calibration (pixels per µm) via Preferences → Calibration.
Enable all metrics (Area, Circularity, etc.) via Preferences → Metrics.
Set Intensity Threshold = 0.2, Window Size = 20, Size Threshold = 80 (good starting values; adjust if necessary).
Click “Apply Settings to All” to segment all images.
Review each image; use the combine tool for over‑split organoids and adjust parameters if needed.
Save the segmented images (File → Save → Image Set).
Export the quantitative data as an Excel file (Image Set → Export Signature).

steps.title: Analyze metrics with OrganoAna
steps.instruction: Analyze the OrganoSeg output using OrganoAna (download from https://github.com/B-P-R-C/Lorenowicz/blob/main/OrganoAna%20-%20ExpectedResults.xlsm) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Open OrganoAna and the OrganoSeg Excel output; type the OrganoSeg file name into “Input file name” and click “Load Data”.
Assign each image to one of up to eight experimental groups (Group1‑Group8).
Set Excel calculation mode to Manual (Formulas → Calculation Options → Manual) to improve responsiveness; remember to switch back to Automatic before final results.
Enter the OrganoSeg parameters used (Intensity Threshold 0.2, Window Size 20, Size Threshold 80, Scale) for record‑keeping.
Select the “Parameter of Interest” (default: average area) from the dropdown menu.
Choose a reference group for normalization in the bar‑graph tab.
Generate the bar graph; a label‑free version is available on the “Fig” sheet for export.

Perform statistical analyses: two‑tailed unequal‑variance Student’s t‑test (Excel TTEST(Array1;Array2;2;3)), Bonferroni‑corrected p‑values, one‑way ANOVA, and Dunnett’s post‑hoc test (two‑tailed, unequal group sizes).
Configure OrganoAna filtering (default values): Circularity 0.5–1.6, Perimeter/A ratio 0.05–0.6, Size > 300 µm²; other parameters (Eccentricity, MeanPixelInt) are left unfiltered.
Be aware of technical limits: maximum 72 images, up to 2000 objects per sheet (≈500 organoids per image plus background), and up to eight experimental conditions.
